problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(1,0),(-1,0),(2,1).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the **clockwise** rotation ${R}_{-\pi }$ by an angle of $\pi $ radians about the origin?

- $(1,0)$
- $(-1,0)$
- $(2,1)$

feedback.problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(2,1),(3,3),(4,4).$  Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the counterclockwise rotation ${R}_{\pi }$ by an angle of $\pi $ radians about the origin?

- $(-2,-1)$
- $(-3,-2)$
- $(-3,-3)$
feedback.worked_solution:
The counterclockwise rotation ${R}_{\pi }$ by an angle of $\pi $ radians is given by the matrix

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of ${R}_{\pi },$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under ${R}_{\pi }$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 & -4 \\ -1 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(-2,-1),(-3,-3),(-4,-4).$

So, the correct answer is "I and III only."
